The assigned probe does not exercise interruption/release recovery across all four current Chapter Two Candy Maker actions; real pause/focus-loss behavior remains unobserved.

play_appeal.hypothesis: Coating, matching, circling, and placing the same five strawberries on the actual cake offer a clear hand-action change while keeping one ingredient and the cake's result in view. The proposed appeal depends on whether the child notices that each action changes those same berries and chooses to continue to decorate the cake; a four-step task could also feel repetitive if the visual changes are too subtle.
play_appeal.appeal_test: On the intended phone, give a child the normal spoken/pictorial invitation without naming the gestures. Observe whether they independently switch from pouring to dragging, circling, and tapping, notice the strawberries becoming cake decorations, and ask to continue or replay. Record confusion, adult prompts, and voluntary replay without converting these observations into a numeric fun score.

observations.title: Chapter Two changes the hand action across four connected berry tasks
evidence: scripts/chapter_two_career_scene_adapter.gd:38-42 defines the Candy Maker workshop's four ordered phases, each reusing the same strawberry and cake story assets with distinct modes and spoken cues.
scripts/opera_career_world_2d.gd:2059-2093 maps the four milestones to distinct visible actions: coating, sorting, glazing, and placing the berries on cake.
observations.reproduction: Resolve the candymaker Chapter Two adapter and inspect its phases in order; match each milestone to _chapter2_candy_visible_action and the corresponding _draw_chapter2_candy_* function.
observations.child_impact: Keeping the same five berries and cake visible while the task changes may help a non-reader understand why each new gesture matters and see cumulative authorship.
observations.proposed_repair: No code repair is indicated by this source review. Observe whether each phase visibly advances the same cake story and whether the changed gesture is independently discoverable.
observations.acceptance_test: In a fresh normal Chapter Two run on the target phone, the child independently performs coat, matching sort, circular glaze, and cake placement in order; each accepted action visibly changes the berries or cake and the child can resume after lifting.

observations.title: Older Syrup path pays only when the ladle truly fills the mold
evidence: scripts/probe_opera_2d.gd:746-779 presses the actual surface grab point, runs 1/30-second steps, releases just before brim, verifies no completion, then holds to completion and verifies exact goal progress.
audit/cycles/luna-playtest-20261012/runtime/L24/attempt_1/probe.log:368-375 records the Syrup threshold, fill, completion picture, empty-ladle settle, and clean SORT handoff assertions passing.

observations.reproduction: In the focused probe, hold the ladle until fill exceeds 0.94 but remains below 1.0, release, verify no completion, then hold at the grab point to brim and process the settle.
observations.child_impact: Progress stays tied to the visible pour and the success state rights an empty ladle, making cause and payoff legible in this scripted geometry.
observations.proposed_repair: None indicated by the bounded probe. Confirm stream visibility and fill response at native phone size before extending the conclusion to device usability.
observations.acceptance_test: At target-phone scale, a child can begin and stop the pour, sees the mold remain unfinished before brim, and sees the ladle settle upright once the completed fill advances to the next activity.

observations.title: Sort recovery keeps a wrong drop from consuming a berry
evidence: scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:4568-4600 checks the released bin against the candy's type; correct drops advance, while incorrect drops reset the same piece without advancing and restart its demonstration.
scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:4686-4714 draws three distinct bins, candy silhouettes, a moving piece, and six progress marks.
observations.reproduction: Start the candy sort, drag the current piece to a visibly wrong bin, release, and check that the same candy returns to its starting position with no increment; then drag it to its matching bin and release.
observations.child_impact: A mistake is recoverable and preserves the objective, which avoids a punitive loss while giving a retry cue.
observations.proposed_repair: No source repair indicated. Check that the color/silhouette distinction and replay hint are understandable without reading on the actual device.
observations.acceptance_test: A child can make a wrong drop, understand the returned candy and demonstrated match, then complete the same piece without losing earlier correct placements.

strengths.claim: The Chapter Two story phases change gesture while preserving one ingredient-to-cake throughline.
Wrong candy drops do not consume the current piece, and passive belt motion loops without advancing the queue.
evidence: scripts/opera_gesture_surface.gd:4536-4544 and :4591-4600; runtime L24 receipt/log confirms the assigned probe completed without failures.

strengths.claim: The active room station is a pointer to the activity, while travel/opening remain separate from scoring.

play_sequence.beat: Find the Candy Maker workshop from its normal Castle-room invitation and approach COAT STRAWBERRIES.
play_sequence.input: Tap the visible Candy Maker trigger once; wait for Roshan's walk and object-opening flourish, then wait for the spoken cue to finish before touching the activity.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child connect the strawberry/candy setting with the invitation and wait for Roshan to arrive?

play_sequence.beat: Coat the five berries with syrup and see their color/state change.
play_sequence.input: Wait for the cue; press and hold the ladle, keep the stream over the berries, and lift once the visual brim/completion response occurs. Wait about one second for the ladle to settle and the next station invitation.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child notice the berries becoming coated and understand why the task changed?

play_sequence.beat: Sort the same berries into matching color/shape lanes.
play_sequence.input: Tap the taffy-press invitation; wait through travel, opening, and cue. Press the moving berry, drag it into a matching lane, and release; repeat for each prompted piece. If a wrong drop happens, wait for the returned piece and demonstration before retrying.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child use color or silhouette matching intentionally and treat a returned piece as a retry rather than a failure?

play_sequence.beat: Glaze the sorted berries with a circular motion.
play_sequence.input: Tap the cottage invitation and wait for arrival/opening/cue. Draw comfortable circles over the candy; lift between attempts if desired and wait for the next hint before resuming. Wait one second after the accepted completion.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the circular gesture feel distinct from sorting, and does the berry/cake visual make the glaze payoff clear?

play_sequence.beat: Place each finished strawberry on the actual cake.
play_sequence.input: Tap the cart invitation; wait for travel/opening/cue. Tap the indicated candy and cake placement anchors one at a time, lifting between taps; after the fifth placement wait for the completed cake reveal to finish.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child see that each tap decorates the same cake and show interest in the finished result?

play_sequence.beat: Offer the normal exit/return and observe whether the child wants another activity or another Candy Maker run.
play_sequence.input: Wait two seconds after the cake result, then make no suggestion; let the child tap a visible exit/return or replay choice if present and wait for the room to settle.
play_sequence.appeal_test: Does the child independently choose what to do next or request the Candy Maker again?

acceptance_gaps: The single assigned internal probe passes, but its Candy Maker syrup leg is the older SYRUP mechanic and it does not play Chapter Two's four COAT/SORT/GLAZE/PLACE story phases to completion.

No fresh-save live-route observation, Mobile capture, physical phone input, touch latency, frame pacing, or child comprehension/replay session was collected; MA-PLAY-001, MA-CHILD-001, MA-OPERA-004, and MA-OPERA-012 remain open at their existing scopes.
The scripted probe checks voice keys/phase data but does not establish recording approval, intelligibility, audibility, or cue timing on device.
